articles.title: The Real Legacy Of Gloria Steinem
articles.author: Carrie Gress
articles.summary: Glowing obituaries are pouring in after the death of feminist icon Gloria Steinem, who was born in 1934. The Associated Press called her “a potent voice of US feminism,” and the Washington Post heralded her as the “lodestar of the modern women’s movement.” It is hard to overstate her influence upon Western women. Gloria Steinem wasn’t just one among many feminists; she was the “it” girl who normalized feminism and made it broadly attractive. Prior to her arrival on the scene, the movement was populated by angry, cantankerous, and mentally ill women whose irascibility made them difficult to work with: Kate Millett was mentally ill and an “out” bisexual; Angela Davis was an angry Black Panther; and Betty Friedan wasn’t the kind of woman other women dreamed of being like. And then came Gloria. Her long blond tresses, aviator glasses, and lithe physique opened the door to a new chapter for feminism. She was articulate, savvy, and a fresh force for the feminist movement. Not everyone appreciated the star power she brought to the movement. This time the company is placing limits on Cloud Gaming, which allows users to play games sans downloads. Beginning in November, those shake out as follows (on a monthly basis): Game Pass Ultimate: 15 hours Game Pass Premium: 10 hours Game Pass Essential: 5 hours Many individual games last longer than 15 hours. But worry not: You can always purchase more hours if you use up your monthly allowance (Microsoft says pricing details will come in November). “We recognize that introducing limits is a meaningful change, particularly for players who regularly spend more time gaming through the cloud,” Team Xbox wrote in a blog post , claiming that this change will impact just four percent of users. “We’re introducing this model because the cost of providing cloud gaming grows as more people use it and play for longer.
